# Test for maybeRetryBoot with globalConfig
#
# This test verifies that when a VM boot fails and is retried via maybeRetryBoot,
# the globalConfig is properly passed during retry.
#
# BACKGROUND:
# ===========
# There was a bug where maybeRetryBoot passed nil for globalConfig instead of
# the actual config. This meant device-wide settings were not applied during
# boot retries.
#
# TEST STRATEGY:
# ==============
# We verify that the VMM memory limit from globalConfig is applied during retry:
#
# 1. Set memory.vmm.limit.MiB=800 (VMM overhead = 800 MB)
# 2. Deploy VM with 1024 MB memory
# 3. Verify cgroup memory limit = 1024 MB + 800 MB overhead = ~1.8 GB
# 4. Delete VM
# 5. Make /run/hypervisor/kvm directory immutable (chattr +i)
# 6. Deploy VM again - DomainCreate will fail, setting BootFailed=true
# 7. Remove immutable flag (chattr -i)
# 8. Wait for maybeRetryBoot to trigger (after timer.boot.retry seconds)
# 9. Verify cgroup memory limit still includes 800 MB overhead
#
# Without the fix: globalConfig=nil, so VMM overhead uses estimatedVMMOverhead() (~374 MB)
# With the fix: globalConfig is passed, so 800 MB overhead is applied
#
# The difference (~400 MB) is large enough to clearly detect the bug.
#
# Note: We use /run/hypervisor/kvm/ because this is where KVM creates domain state.
# Corrupting this causes failure in DomainCreate, which sets BootFailed=true.
#
# PREREQUISITES:
# ==============
# - EVE image with the maybeRetryBoot fix (globalConfig passed correctly)
# - EVE with KVM support
#
# RECOMMENDED: Use the wrapper script for setup and execution:
#   cd <eden-repo>
#   ./run-boot-retry-test.sh [EVE_TAG]
#
# The wrapper script handles:
#   - Environment cleanup (eden stop/clean)
#   - Eden build and configuration
#   - EVE setup/start/onboard
#   - Test execution with logging
#
# For manual setup (not recommended):
#   cd <eden-repo>
#   make build-tests
#   ./eden config add default --force
#   ./eden config set default --key eve.tag --value "<your-eve-tag>"
#   ./eden setup && ./eden start && ./eden eve onboard
#   ./eden test tests/eclient -v debug -t 20m -e boot_retry_globalconfig
#

{{$network_name := "boot-retry-n1"}}
{{$test_app := "retry-test-vm"}}
{{$port := "2223"}}
{{define "ubuntu_image"}}https://cloud-images.ubuntu.com/releases/focal/release-20210510/ubuntu-20.04-server-cloudimg-amd64.img{{end}}

[!exec:bash] stop
[!exec:sleep] stop
[!exec:chmod] stop

exec chmod 600 {{EdenConfig "eden.tests"}}/eclient/image/cert/id_rsa

message 'Starting Boot Retry globalConfig Test'


# ============================================================================
# SETUP: Configure logging, retry interval and VMM memory limit
# ============================================================================

# Enable debug logging for domainmgr to see maybeRetryBoot messages
message 'Enabling debug logging for domainmgr...'
eden controller edge-node update --config debug.domainmgr.loglevel=debug

message 'Configuring boot retry interval to 60 seconds (default is 600)'
eden controller edge-node update --config timer.boot.retry=60

message 'Configuring VMM memory limit to 800 MiB'
eden controller edge-node update --config memory.vmm.limit.MiB=800

# Wait for config to be applied (extra time for fresh EVE after onboarding)
exec sleep 30

# Verify config is applied
exec -t 3m bash wait-config-applied.sh timer.boot.retry 60
exec -t 3m bash wait-config-applied.sh memory.vmm.limit.MiB 800

# ============================================================================
# SETUP: Create network
# ============================================================================
message 'Creating network boot-retry-n1'
eden -t 1m network create 10.11.12.0/24 -n {{$network_name}}
test eden.network.test -test.v -timewait 2m ACTIVATED {{$network_name}}

# ============================================================================
# TC1: Deploy VM and verify initial VMM memory limit
# ============================================================================
message '=== TC1: Deploy VM and verify VMM memory limit from globalConfig ==='

# Deploy the VM - it should start successfully
message 'Deploying VM...'
eden pod deploy -n {{$test_app}} --memory=1024MB --vnc-display=1 -p {{$port}}:22 {{template "ubuntu_image"}} --networks={{$network_name}}

# Wait for VM to be running
message 'Waiting for VM to start...'
exec -t 10m bash wait-for-running-once.sh {{$test_app}}
message 'VM is running'

# Give it extra time to stabilize
exec sleep 10

# Verify initial cgroup memory limit includes 800 MiB overhead
# Expected: 1024 MB * 1024 + 800 MiB * 1024 * 1024 = 1048576000 + 838860800 = 1887436800 bytes
message 'Verifying initial cgroup memory limit...'
exec -t 1m bash verify-cgroup-memory.sh {{$test_app}} 1887436800
message 'Initial VMM memory limit verified (800 MiB overhead applied)'

# ============================================================================
# TC2: Cause boot failure and verify retry uses globalConfig
# ============================================================================
message '=== TC2: Cause boot failure to trigger maybeRetryBoot ==='

# Delete the VM first - we need a fresh deploy to trigger DomainCreate
# (stop/start only resumes, it doesn't call DomainCreate)
message 'Deleting VM to prepare for fresh deploy...'
eden pod delete {{$test_app}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 2m - {{$test_app}}
message 'VM deleted'

# Make KVM state directory immutable to cause DomainCreate failure
message 'Making KVM state directory immutable...'
exec -t 1m bash make-kvm-dir-immutable.sh

# Deploy the VM again - DomainCreate will fail because it can't create state directory
message 'Deploying VM (will fail due to immutable KVM state directory)...'
eden pod deploy -n {{$test_app}} --memory=1024MB --vnc-display=1 -p {{$port}}:22 {{template "ubuntu_image"}} --networks={{$network_name}}

# Wait for boot failure (3 attempts, then BootFailed=true)
message 'Waiting for boot failure (3 attempts)...'
exec -t 10m bash wait-for-boot-failure.sh {{$test_app}}

# Restore the directory so retry can succeed
message 'Restoring KVM state directory...'
exec -t 1m bash make-kvm-dir-writable.sh

# ============================================================================
# TC3: Wait for maybeRetryBoot and verify globalConfig is applied
# ============================================================================
message '=== TC3: Wait for boot retry and verify VMM memory limit ==='

# maybeRetryBoot triggers after timer.boot.retry seconds (60s)
message 'Waiting for retry timer...'
exec sleep 70

# Now wait for the VM to restart
exec -t 5m bash wait-for-running-once.sh {{$test_app}}
message 'VM started successfully via maybeRetryBoot!'

# Verify that maybeRetryBoot was actually called by checking EVE logs
message 'Verifying maybeRetryBoot was triggered in EVE logs...'
exec -t 1m bash verify-retry-logs.sh {{$test_app}}

# Verify cgroup memory limit still includes 800 MiB overhead
# This proves globalConfig was passed to Setup during retry
message 'Verifying cgroup memory limit after retry...'
exec -t 1m bash verify-cgroup-memory.sh {{$test_app}} 1887436800
message 'SUCCESS: VMM memory limit from globalConfig applied during retry!'

# ============================================================================
# CLEANUP
# ============================================================================
message '=== Cleanup ==='

eden pod delete {{$test_app}}
test eden.app.test -test.v -timewait 2m - {{$test_app}}

eden network delete {{$network_name}}
test eden.network.test -test.v -timewait 2m - {{$network_name}}

# Reset config to defaults
eden controller edge-node update --config timer.boot.retry=600
eden controller edge-node update --config memory.vmm.limit.MiB=0
eden controller edge-node update --config debug.domainmgr.loglevel=info

message '=== Test Complete ==='

-- eden-config.yml --
{{/* Test config file */}}
test:
    controller: adam://{{EdenConfig "adam.ip"}}:{{EdenConfig "adam.port"}}
    eve:
      {{EdenConfig "eve.name"}}:
        onboard-cert: {{EdenConfigPath "eve.cert"}}
        serial: "{{EdenConfig "eve.serial"}}"
        model: {{EdenConfig "eve.devmodel"}}

-- wait-config-applied.sh --
#!/bin/bash
# Wait for a config value to be applied in EVE
# $1 = config key (e.g., "timer.boot.retry")
# $2 = expected value (e.g., "60")
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}
CONFIG_KEY="$1"
EXPECTED_VALUE="$2"

echo "=== Waiting for config '$CONFIG_KEY' to be set to '$EXPECTED_VALUE' ==="

MAX_ATTEMPTS=60
POLL_INTERVAL=3

for ATTEMPT in $(seq 1 $MAX_ATTEMPTS); do
    # Read ConfigItemValueMap from EVE (correct path: /persist/status/zedagent/)
    RAW_OUTPUT=$($EDEN eve ssh "cat /persist/status/zedagent/ConfigItemValueMap/global.json 2>/dev/null" 2>/dev/null || echo "")

    # Try to extract the value - handle both IntValue and StrValue
    KEY_SECTION=$(echo "$RAW_OUTPUT" | grep -o "\"$CONFIG_KEY\"[^}]*}" | head -1)

    INT_VALUE=$(echo "$KEY_SECTION" | grep -o '"IntValue":[0-9]*' | sed 's/"IntValue"://')
    STR_VALUE=$(echo "$KEY_SECTION" | grep -o '"StrValue":"[^"]*"' | sed 's/"StrValue":"//; s/"$//')

    if [ -n "$STR_VALUE" ]; then
        CURRENT_VALUE="$STR_VALUE"
    elif [ -n "$INT_VALUE" ]; then
        CURRENT_VALUE="$INT_VALUE"
    else
        CURRENT_VALUE=""
    fi

    echo "Attempt $ATTEMPT/$MAX_ATTEMPTS: Current value for '$CONFIG_KEY': '$CURRENT_VALUE'"

    if [ "$CURRENT_VALUE" = "$EXPECTED_VALUE" ]; then
        echo "SUCCESS: Config '$CONFIG_KEY' is set to '$EXPECTED_VALUE'"
        exit 0
    fi

    sleep $POLL_INTERVAL
done

echo "ERROR: Timeout waiting for config '$CONFIG_KEY' to be set to '$EXPECTED_VALUE'"
echo "Current value: '$CURRENT_VALUE'"
exit 1

-- wait-for-running-once.sh --
#!/bin/bash
# Wait for a pod to reach RUNNING state
# $1 = pod name
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}
POD_NAME="$1"

echo "=== Waiting for pod '$POD_NAME' to reach RUNNING state ==="
echo "Polling every 5 seconds..."

MAX_ATTEMPTS=60
POLL_INTERVAL=5

for ATTEMPT in $(seq 1 $MAX_ATTEMPTS); do
    STATE=$($EDEN pod ps 2>/dev/null | grep "^$POD_NAME" | awk '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i ~ /RUNNING|HALTED|BOOTING|INSTALLED|BROKEN|ERROR/) print $i}' | head -1)

    echo "Attempt $ATTEMPT/$MAX_ATTEMPTS: Pod '$POD_NAME' state: $STATE"

    if [ "$STATE" = "RUNNING" ]; then
        echo "SUCCESS: Pod '$POD_NAME' reached RUNNING state!"
        exit 0
    fi

    sleep $POLL_INTERVAL
done

echo "ERROR: Timeout waiting for pod '$POD_NAME' to reach RUNNING state"
exit 1

-- verify-cgroup-memory.sh --
#!/bin/bash
# Verify the cgroup memory limit for a pod matches expected value
# $1 = pod name
# $2 = expected memory limit in bytes
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}
POD_NAME="$1"
EXPECTED_LIMIT="$2"

echo "=== Verifying cgroup memory limit for pod '$POD_NAME' ==="
echo "Expected limit: $EXPECTED_LIMIT bytes"

# Get the pod UUID
VM_UUID=$($EDEN pod ps 2>/dev/null | awk -v name="$POD_NAME" '$1==name {print $3}' | head -1)
if [ -z "$VM_UUID" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: Could not find UUID for pod '$POD_NAME'"
    exit 1
fi
echo "Pod UUID: $VM_UUID"

# Find the cgroup memory limit
CGROUP_PATH="/sys/fs/cgroup/memory/eve-user-apps/${VM_UUID}.1.1/memory.limit_in_bytes"
echo "Checking cgroup path: $CGROUP_PATH"

ACTUAL_LIMIT=$($EDEN eve ssh "cat $CGROUP_PATH 2>/dev/null" 2>/dev/null)

if [ -z "$ACTUAL_LIMIT" ]; then
    # Try with different suffix
    CGROUP_PATH="/sys/fs/cgroup/memory/eve-user-apps/${VM_UUID}.1.2/memory.limit_in_bytes"
    ACTUAL_LIMIT=$($EDEN eve ssh "cat $CGROUP_PATH 2>/dev/null" 2>/dev/null)
fi

if [ -z "$ACTUAL_LIMIT" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: Could not read cgroup memory limit"
    echo "Searching for cgroup..."
    $EDEN eve ssh "find /sys/fs/cgroup/memory -name '*${VM_UUID}*' 2>/dev/null" 2>/dev/null
    exit 1
fi

echo "Actual limit: $ACTUAL_LIMIT bytes"

# Allow 5% tolerance for rounding
TOLERANCE=80000000
DIFF=$((ACTUAL_LIMIT - EXPECTED_LIMIT))
if [ $DIFF -lt 0 ]; then
    DIFF=$((-DIFF))
fi

if [ $DIFF -le $TOLERANCE ]; then
    echo "SUCCESS: Memory limit matches expected value (within tolerance)"
    echo "Expected: $EXPECTED_LIMIT, Actual: $ACTUAL_LIMIT, Diff: $DIFF"
    exit 0
fi

echo "ERROR: Memory limit mismatch!"
echo "Expected: $EXPECTED_LIMIT bytes"
echo "Actual: $ACTUAL_LIMIT bytes"
echo "Difference: $DIFF bytes (tolerance: $TOLERANCE)"
exit 1

-- wait-for-halted.sh --
#!/bin/bash
# Wait for a pod to reach HALTED state (after eden pod stop)
# $1 = pod name
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}
POD_NAME="$1"

echo "=== Waiting for pod '$POD_NAME' to reach HALTED state ==="
echo "Polling every 5 seconds..."

MAX_ATTEMPTS=36
POLL_INTERVAL=5

for ATTEMPT in $(seq 1 $MAX_ATTEMPTS); do
    STATE=$($EDEN pod ps 2>/dev/null | grep "^$POD_NAME" | awk '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i ~ /RUNNING|HALTED|HALTING|BOOTING|INSTALLED|BROKEN|ERROR/) print $i}' | head -1)

    echo "Attempt $ATTEMPT/$MAX_ATTEMPTS: Pod '$POD_NAME' state: $STATE"

    if [ "$STATE" = "HALTED" ]; then
        echo "SUCCESS: Pod '$POD_NAME' reached HALTED state!"
        exit 0
    fi

    # Also accept if the pod disappeared or is in ERROR/BROKEN (fully stopped)
    if [ -z "$STATE" ] || [ "$STATE" = "ERROR" ] || [ "$STATE" = "BROKEN" ]; then
        echo "Pod '$POD_NAME' is in state '$STATE' (treating as stopped)"
        exit 0
    fi

    sleep $POLL_INTERVAL
done

echo "ERROR: Timeout waiting for pod '$POD_NAME' to reach HALTED state"
echo "Last state: $STATE"
exit 1

-- wait-for-boot-failure.sh --
#!/bin/bash
# Wait for a pod to attempt boot and fail (enter ERROR or BROKEN state, or have an error message)
# This waits for image download to complete first, then for the boot failure
# IMPORTANT: Fails immediately if VM reaches RUNNING state (means corruption didn't work)
# $1 = pod name
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}
POD_NAME="$1"

echo "=== Waiting for pod '$POD_NAME' to attempt boot and fail ==="
echo "This will wait for image download first, then for boot failure..."
echo "NOTE: Will fail immediately if VM reaches RUNNING state (corruption didn't work)"

MAX_ATTEMPTS=120
POLL_INTERVAL=5

for ATTEMPT in $(seq 1 $MAX_ATTEMPTS); do
    # Get the full line for the pod
    POD_LINE=$($EDEN pod ps 2>/dev/null | grep "^$POD_NAME" || echo "")

    # Extract state
    STATE=$(echo "$POD_LINE" | awk '{for(i=1;i<=NF;i++) if($i ~ /RUNNING|HALTED|HALTING|BOOTING|INSTALLED|BROKEN|ERROR/) print $i}' | head -1)

    echo "Attempt $ATTEMPT/$MAX_ATTEMPTS: Pod '$POD_NAME' state: $STATE"

    # FAIL EARLY: If VM is RUNNING, our corruption didn't work!
    if [ "$STATE" = "RUNNING" ]; then
        echo ""
        echo "ERROR: Pod '$POD_NAME' reached RUNNING state!"
        echo "This means the OVMF directory corruption did not prevent boot."
        echo "Check if chattr +i was applied correctly."
        echo ""
        echo "Checking OVMF directory status..."
        $EDEN eve ssh "ls -la /persist/vault/ovmf/ 2>/dev/null; lsattr /persist/vault/ovmf/ 2>/dev/null" 2>/dev/null || true
        exit 1
    fi

    # Check for error states that indicate boot failure
    if [ "$STATE" = "ERROR" ] || [ "$STATE" = "BROKEN" ]; then
        echo "SUCCESS: Pod '$POD_NAME' is in failed state '$STATE' - boot failure detected!"
        exit 0
    fi

    # Check for error message in the output (e.g., "HALTING: [description:...")
    if echo "$POD_LINE" | grep -qE "error|Error|ERROR|failed|Failed|FAILED"; then
        echo "SUCCESS: Pod '$POD_NAME' has error message - boot failure detected!"
        echo "Pod line: $POD_LINE"
        exit 0
    fi

    # If pod is in HALTED state (not HALTING), boot was attempted and stopped
    if [ "$STATE" = "HALTED" ]; then
        echo "SUCCESS: Pod '$POD_NAME' is HALTED - boot failure detected!"
        exit 0
    fi

    sleep $POLL_INTERVAL
done

echo "WARNING: Timeout waiting for boot failure, continuing anyway..."
echo "Last state: $STATE"
# Don't fail - maybe the boot failure happened but we missed it
exit 0


-- verify-fml-resolution.sh --
#!/bin/bash
# Verify FML resolution is correctly applied to a VM
# $1 = pod name
# $2 = expected resolution (e.g., "1024x768")
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}
POD_NAME="$1"
EXPECTED_RES="$2"

echo "=== Verifying FML resolution for pod '$POD_NAME' ==="
echo "Expected resolution: $EXPECTED_RES"

VM_UUID=$($EDEN pod ps 2>/dev/null | awk -v name="$POD_NAME" '$1==name {print $3}' | head -1)
if [ -n "$VM_UUID" ]; then
    echo "Pod UUID: $VM_UUID"
fi

# Method 1: Look for OVMF vars/settings file name containing the resolution (most stable)
echo ""
echo "Method 1: Checking OVMF settings files..."
OVMF_FILES=$($EDEN eve ssh "ls -la /persist/vault/ovmf-settings/ 2>/dev/null | grep -F '$EXPECTED_RES'" 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ -n "$OVMF_FILES" ]; then
    echo "$OVMF_FILES"
    echo "SUCCESS: OVMF settings file exists for resolution '$EXPECTED_RES'"
    exit 0
fi

# Method 2: Check QEMU cmdline for uuid + resolution token in any file path
# (best-effort; depends on how qemu args look)
echo ""
echo "Method 2: Checking QEMU cmdline..."
if [ -n "$VM_UUID" ]; then
    QEMU_LINE=$($EDEN eve ssh "ps aux | grep '[q]emu-system-x86_64' | grep -F '$VM_UUID' | head -1" 2>/dev/null || true)
else
    QEMU_LINE=$($EDEN eve ssh "ps aux | grep '[q]emu-system-x86_64' | head -1" 2>/dev/null || true)
fi

echo "$QEMU_LINE"
if echo "$QEMU_LINE" | grep -Fq "$EXPECTED_RES"; then
    echo "SUCCESS: QEMU cmdline contains resolution '$EXPECTED_RES'"
    exit 0
fi

# Method 3: Fallback to global config (this verifies config propagation even if
# we can't see OVMF artifacts)
echo ""
echo "Method 3: Verifying global FML resolution config..."
GLOBAL_RES=$($EDEN eve ssh "cat /persist/status/zedagent/ConfigItemValueMap/global.json 2>/dev/null" 2>/dev/null | grep -o '"app.fml.resolution"[^}]*' | grep -o '"StrValue":"[^"]*"' | sed 's/"StrValue":"//; s/"$//')

echo "Global FML resolution config: '$GLOBAL_RES'"
if [ "$GLOBAL_RES" = "$EXPECTED_RES" ]; then
    echo "Global config shows correct resolution (treating as success)"
    exit 0
fi

echo "ERROR: Could not verify FML resolution '$EXPECTED_RES' was applied"
exit 1

-- verify-retry-logs.sh --
#!/bin/bash
# Verify that maybeRetryBoot was actually triggered by checking EVE logs
# $1 = pod name
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}
POD_NAME="$1"

echo "=== Verifying maybeRetryBoot was triggered for pod '$POD_NAME' ==="

# Get the pod UUID
VM_UUID=$($EDEN pod ps 2>/dev/null | awk -v name="$POD_NAME" '$1==name {print $3}' | head -1)
echo "Pod UUID: $VM_UUID"

# Check EVE logs for maybeRetryBoot messages
# The log messages we're looking for (from domainmgr.go):
# - "maybeRetryBoot(%s) after %s at %v" - when retry is triggered
# - "maybeRetryBoot(%s) DONE for %s" - when retry completes successfully
echo ""
echo "Searching EVE logs for maybeRetryBoot messages..."

RETRY_LOGS=$($EDEN eve ssh "logread 2>/dev/null | grep -i 'maybeRetryBoot' | tail -20" 2>/dev/null || echo "")

if [ -z "$RETRY_LOGS" ]; then
    echo "WARNING: No maybeRetryBoot messages found in logs"
    echo ""
    echo "Checking for BootFailed messages instead..."
    BOOT_FAILED_LOGS=$($EDEN eve ssh "logread 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'BootFailed|boot.*failed|failed.*boot' | tail -10" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
    if [ -n "$BOOT_FAILED_LOGS" ]; then
        echo "Found BootFailed messages:"
        echo "$BOOT_FAILED_LOGS"
    fi

    echo ""
    echo "Checking for domain retry messages..."
    DOMAIN_LOGS=$($EDEN eve ssh "logread 2>/dev/null | grep -iE 'retry|Retry' | grep -i domain | tail -10" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
    if [ -n "$DOMAIN_LOGS" ]; then
        echo "Found domain retry messages:"
        echo "$DOMAIN_LOGS"
    fi

    # Don't fail - logs might have rotated or we might have missed the window
    echo ""
    echo "WARNING: Could not find explicit maybeRetryBoot logs, but VM started successfully"
    echo "This may indicate logs rotated or different log format"
    exit 0
fi

echo "Found maybeRetryBoot messages:"
echo "$RETRY_LOGS"

# Check if the logs contain our pod's UUID
if [ -n "$VM_UUID" ] && echo "$RETRY_LOGS" | grep -qF "$VM_UUID"; then
    echo ""
    echo "SUCCESS: Found maybeRetryBoot log entry for pod UUID '$VM_UUID'"
    exit 0
fi

# Check for "DONE" message indicating successful retry
if echo "$RETRY_LOGS" | grep -q "DONE"; then
    echo ""
    echo "SUCCESS: Found maybeRetryBoot DONE message - retry completed successfully"
    exit 0
fi

echo ""
echo "SUCCESS: maybeRetryBoot was triggered (found log entries)"
exit 0

-- make-kvm-dir-immutable.sh --
#!/bin/bash
# Make the KVM state directory immutable to cause DomainCreate failure
# EVE creates /run/hypervisor/kvm/<domain-name>/ during domain creation
# If the parent directory is immutable, mkdir fails, causing BootFailed=true
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}

echo "=== Making KVM state directory immutable to cause boot failure ==="

# Create the directory if it doesn't exist, then make it immutable
RESULT=$($EDEN eve ssh "mkdir -p /run/hypervisor/kvm && chattr +i /run/hypervisor/kvm && echo 'Directory made immutable'" 2>&1)

echo "$RESULT"

if echo "$RESULT" | grep -q "immutable"; then
    echo "SUCCESS: KVM state directory is now immutable, DomainCreate will fail"
    exit 0
fi

echo "ERROR: Failed to make KVM state directory immutable"
exit 1

-- make-kvm-dir-writable.sh --
#!/bin/bash
# Remove immutable flag from KVM state directory so boot retry can succeed
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}

echo "=== Removing immutable flag from KVM state directory ==="

# Remove immutable flag from /run/hypervisor/kvm
RESULT=$($EDEN eve ssh "chattr -i /run/hypervisor/kvm && echo 'Directory made writable'" 2>&1)

echo "$RESULT"

if echo "$RESULT" | grep -q "writable"; then
    echo "SUCCESS: KVM state directory is now writable, retry will succeed"
    exit 0
fi

echo "ERROR: Failed to make KVM state directory writable"
exit 1

-- make-ovmf-readonly.sh --
#!/bin/bash
# Make the OVMF destination directory immutable to cause VM boot failure
# The copy from /hostfs/etc/ovmf/OVMF_VARS_<resolution>.fd to
# /persist/vault/ovmf/<uuid>_OVMF_VARS.fd will fail
# Note: We use chattr +i because chmod 555 doesn't stop root from writing
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}

echo "=== Making OVMF destination directory immutable to cause boot failure ==="

# Create the directory if it doesn't exist, then make it immutable
RESULT=$($EDEN eve ssh "mkdir -p /persist/vault/ovmf && chattr +i /persist/vault/ovmf && echo 'Directory made immutable'" 2>&1)

echo "$RESULT"

if echo "$RESULT" | grep -q "immutable"; then
    echo "SUCCESS: OVMF directory is now immutable, copy will fail"
    exit 0
fi

echo "ERROR: Failed to make OVMF directory immutable"
exit 1

-- make-ovmf-writable.sh --
#!/bin/bash
# Remove immutable flag from OVMF destination directory so boot retry can succeed
EDEN={{EdenConfig "eden.root"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.bin-dist"}}/{{EdenConfig "eden.eden-bin"}}

echo "=== Removing immutable flag from OVMF destination directory ==="

# Remove immutable flag from /persist/vault/ovmf
RESULT=$($EDEN eve ssh "chattr -i /persist/vault/ovmf && echo 'Directory made writable'" 2>&1)

echo "$RESULT"

if echo "$RESULT" | grep -q "writable"; then
    echo "SUCCESS: OVMF directory is now writable, retry will succeed"
    exit 0
fi

echo "ERROR: Failed to make OVMF directory writable"
exit 1
